newsitem.title: RUSSIA: TENNIS-RUSEDSKI INJURED, FRENCH YOUNGSTER PROFITS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RUSEDSKI INJURED, FRENCH YOUNGSTER PROFITS.

text.p: British number two Greg Rusedski pulled out of the St. Petersburg Open after new problems with the left wrist he injured against Pete Sampras in last month's San Jose final.
Arnaud Clement, a 19-year-old French qualifier ranked 280th in the world, profited from Rusedski's woes and marched into the third round without winning a match.
Clement's first-round opponent, Andrei Olkhovsky, withdrew with a knee injury after losing the first set to the Frenchman on Tuesday.
Even so, Olkhovsky went on to win his first round doubles match with New Zealander Brett Steven.
The Russian explained he pulled out of the singles as soon as he felt the first twinge in the left knee, injured in Copenhagen last week, so as not to let down his doubles partner.
